Aftermath leads all registers at nine entries, with vigil, endurance, defiance, menace, and suspension each between four and six, reckoning at three entries and still unable to score above 1, and reprieve, fury, and interiority untouched. Reckoning keeps illustrating juridical weight rather than finding the object that displaces it. The boundary-object device — wall as knowledge threshold, drafting sheet as erasure field, ledger bisected by shadow — is the most structurally generative move in recent work and points toward one underlying opportunity: a surface that divides legibility rather than space, separating the counted from the erased.

The corpus is technically accomplished and increasingly self-consistent, and the next image that scores above 2 will need to refuse its most available move at the first decision, not the last.
